prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

In spite of the large number of papers appeared in the past which are devoted to the lattice Boltzmann (LB) methods, basic aspects of the theory still remain unchallenged. An unsolved theoretical issue is related to the construction of a discrete kinetic theory which yields \textit{exactly} the fluid equations, i.e., is non-asymptotic (here denoted as \textit{LB inverse kinetic theory}). The purpose of this paper is theoretical and aims at developing an inverse kinetic approach of this type. In principle infinite solutions exist to this problem but the freedom can be exploited in order to meet important requirements. In particular, the discrete kinetic theory can be defined so that it yields exactly the fluid equation also for arbitrary non-equilibrium (but suitably smooth) kinetic distribution functions and arbitrarily close to the boundary of the fluid domain. Unlike previous entropic LB methods the theorem can be obtained without functional constraints on the class of the initial distribution functions. Possible realizations of the theory and asymptotic approximations are provided which permit to determine the fluid equations \textit{with prescribed accuracy.} As a result, asymptotic accuracy estimates of customary LB approaches and comparisons with the Chorin artificial compressibility method are discussed.

outputs.L1: Despite the large number of papers devoted to lattice Boltzmann (LB) methods published to date, fundamental aspects of the theory remain unresolved. One such theoretical issue concerns the construction of a discrete kinetic theory that yields the fluid equations \textit{exactly}, i.e., non-asymptotically (here referred to as \textit{LB inverse kinetic theory}). This paper is theoretical in scope and aims to develop an inverse kinetic approach of this kind. In principle, infinitely many solutions to this problem exist, and the resulting freedom can be exploited to satisfy important requirements. In particular, the discrete kinetic theory can be formulated to recover the fluid equations exactly, even for arbitrary non-equilibrium—though suitably smooth—kinetic distribution functions and at points arbitrarily close to the boundary of the fluid domain. Unlike previous entropic LB methods, the theorem can be established without imposing functional constraints on the class of initial distribution functions. Possible realizations of the theory, together with asymptotic approximations, are presented, allowing the fluid equations to be determined \textit{with prescribed accuracy}. Consequently, asymptotic accuracy estimates for customary LB approaches are discussed, along with comparisons to Chorin’s artificial compressibility method.
outputs.L2: Despite the extensive literature devoted to lattice Boltzmann (LB) methods, several fundamental theoretical questions remain unresolved. One such problem is the formulation of a discrete kinetic theory that reproduces the fluid equations \textit{exactly}, rather than only asymptotically; this is referred to here as \textit{LB inverse kinetic theory}. This paper presents a theoretical framework for developing such an inverse kinetic formulation. Although the problem admits, in principle, infinitely many solutions, this flexibility can be used to satisfy key requirements. Specifically, the discrete kinetic model may be constructed to recover the fluid equations exactly for arbitrary, sufficiently smooth, non-equilibrium kinetic distribution functions, including at points arbitrarily close to the boundary of the fluid domain. In contrast to earlier entropic LB methods, the resulting theorem does not require functional restrictions on the class of admissible initial distribution functions. The paper also describes possible implementations and asymptotic approximations that enable the fluid equations to be determined \textit{with prescribed accuracy}. Finally, it examines asymptotic error estimates for conventional LB schemes and compares them with Chorin’s artificial compressibility method.
outputs.L3:
The paper addresses the unresolved challenge of constructing a non-asymptotic lattice Boltzmann inverse kinetic theory that reproduces the target fluid equations exactly. Although the inverse problem admits infinitely many solutions, this non-uniqueness is advantageous: the available degrees of freedom can be exploited to satisfy key theoretical and practical requirements.

The proposed discrete kinetic theory remains exact for arbitrary, sufficiently smooth non-equilibrium distribution functions, including in regions close to the boundaries of the fluid domain. In contrast to earlier entropic lattice Boltzmann methods, it does not impose functional restrictions on the initial distribution functions, thereby allowing greater flexibility in the specification of initial data.

The paper also develops explicit realizations of the theory and derives asymptotic approximations with prescribed levels of accuracy. These results include error estimates for standard lattice Boltzmann approaches and a comparison with Chorin’s artificial compressibility method, clarifying the relationships, limitations, and accuracy of the respective formulations.
outputs.L4:
The paper presents a non-asymptotic lattice Boltzmann inverse kinetic theory for the exact representation of fluid dynamics. Unlike conventional lattice Boltzmann approaches, which generally recover the target macroscopic equations only in a suitable asymptotic limit, the proposed framework is constructed so that the relevant velocity moments of the kinetic equations reproduce the prescribed fluid equations exactly. This correspondence is intended to remain valid without requiring the distribution functions to be close to equilibrium and also applies to smooth non-equilibrium distributions in the vicinity of boundaries.

A central feature of the inverse kinetic formulation is that the kinetic evolution and its source or collision terms are designed from the desired macroscopic equations rather than introduced through a fixed microscopic model. The resulting theory therefore does not depend on restrictive assumptions about the initial kinetic distributions. Provided that their moments satisfy the required macroscopic initial data, the distributions may otherwise be chosen with considerable freedom. Boundary conditions can likewise be formulated consistently at the kinetic level while preserving the intended fluid behavior.

The work also discusses practical realizations of the exact theory. Although the inverse kinetic model supplies a non-asymptotic correspondence with the fluid equations, it can be simplified into computationally convenient schemes. Systematic approximations yield algorithms with a prescribed and controllable order of accuracy, making it possible to balance exactness, numerical complexity, and computational cost. In this way, the framework serves both as an exact kinetic representation and as a basis for constructing approximate lattice Boltzmann methods whose errors can be identified and controlled.

Because the target equations are recovered directly through the moment equations, the approach provides a useful benchmark for evaluating more conventional lattice Boltzmann schemes. Their accuracy can be assessed by comparing their asymptotic macroscopic behavior with the exact inverse kinetic representation. The same framework also permits comparison with Chorin’s artificial compressibility method, particularly with respect to the treatment of incompressibility, pressure evolution, and approximation errors.

Overall, the paper establishes that lattice Boltzmann inverse kinetic theories can reproduce fluid equations without relying on asymptotic closure, near-equilibrium assumptions, or specially constrained initial distributions. At the same time, they admit implementable approximations of prescribed accuracy and offer a systematic basis for comparing lattice Boltzmann algorithms with established numerical methods for incompressible fluid flow.
outputs.L5:
### Boltzmann and the Arrow of Time

Ludwig Boltzmann transformed physics by explaining how the behavior of countless microscopic particles produces macroscopic properties such as temperature and pressure. **The** foundation of his work was statistical mechanics, which treats physical laws in terms of probabilities rather than tracking every particle individually.

**Unlike** many of his contemporaries, Boltzmann argued that the second law of thermodynamics is statistical, not absolute. Entropy usually increases because disordered states are overwhelmingly more probable than ordered ones. Although his ideas were controversial during his lifetime, Boltzmann’s insights now shape modern physics and our understanding of time, matter, and the universe.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract for a theoretical paper proposing a non-asymptotic lattice Boltzmann inverse kinetic theory that exactly recovers the fluid equations.
counterfactuals.output: We propose a non-asymptotic inverse kinetic formulation of the lattice Boltzmann method that recovers the target fluid equations exactly at the level of hydrodynamic moments. Rather than deriving macroscopic dynamics through a Chapman–Enskog expansion or a small-Knudsen-number limit, the kinetic populations, discrete velocities, collision operator, and forcing terms are constructed directly from the prescribed fluid system. The resulting moment equations coincide with the continuity and momentum equations without truncation errors associated with asymptotic multiscale expansions. We establish sufficient conditions for realizability, moment closure, conservation, and consistency on a finite velocity lattice, and characterize the non-uniqueness of the underlying kinetic representation. The framework accommodates general equations of state, viscous stresses, body forces, and spatially and temporally varying transport coefficients. Its relation to conventional lattice Boltzmann schemes is clarified by identifying standard models as asymptotic approximations to a broader exact inverse construction. This theory provides a systematic foundation for designing lattice kinetic algorithms whose macroscopic fidelity is imposed a priori, while separating errors due to kinetic representation, spatial discretization, time integration, and boundary treatment.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a research-paper abstract on unresolved theoretical issues in lattice Boltzmann methods, emphasizing exact recovery of fluid equations, infinitely many possible inverse kinetic solutions, and prescribed-accuracy asymptotic approximations.
counterfactuals.output: **Abstract—**Despite the widespread success of lattice Boltzmann methods (LBMs), their theoretical foundations remain incomplete in several respects. This paper examines three closely related unresolved issues. First, we distinguish asymptotic consistency with the Navier–Stokes equations from their exact recovery at finite lattice spacing and time step. Standard Chapman–Enskog and equivalent-equation analyses generally establish only order-dependent approximations, leaving open the conditions under which discrete kinetic dynamics can reproduce prescribed fluid equations exactly, including their initial and boundary data. Second, we consider the inverse kinetic problem: constructing lattice populations, equilibria, collision operators, and forcing terms that yield a specified macroscopic system. Because macroscopic moments constrain only part of the kinetic state, this inverse problem is fundamentally non-unique, admitting infinitely many kinetic realizations with identical target equations but potentially different stability, positivity, isotropy, and boundary behavior. Third, we formulate recovery as a prescribed-accuracy problem rather than an all-or-nothing correspondence. By organizing free kinetic moments and lattice corrections order by order, one may design families of LBMs whose modified equations approximate the desired continuum dynamics to a chosen asymptotic order. The analysis highlights the need to characterize equivalence classes of inverse kinetic solutions, identify compatibility conditions for exact recovery, and separate formal asymptotic accuracy from convergence and nonlinear stability. These questions provide a framework for developing lattice Boltzmann schemes with mathematically controlled macroscopic fidelity.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain, in formal scientific prose, how an inverse kinetic lattice Boltzmann theory could improve upon entropic LB methods and compare its asymptotic accuracy with the Chorin artificial compressibility method.
counterfactuals.output:
An inverse kinetic lattice Boltzmann theory (IKLBT) reverses the usual logic of lattice Boltzmann modeling. Rather than selecting a discrete equilibrium distribution and then determining which macroscopic equations emerge through a Chapman–Enskog expansion, it prescribes the target incompressible Navier–Stokes equations and constructs the kinetic streaming and forcing operators so that the required velocity moments reproduce those equations exactly.

For an incompressible fluid,
\[
\nabla\!\cdot\mathbf{u}=0,
\qquad
\partial_t\mathbf{u}+\mathbf{u}\!\cdot\nabla\mathbf{u}
=-\rho_0^{-1}\nabla p+\nu\nabla^2\mathbf{u}+\mathbf{f},
\]
an inverse kinetic formulation defines populations \(f_i\) on a velocity lattice such that selected moments give the density or pressure and momentum, for example
\[
\sum_i f_i \sim p,\qquad
\sum_i \mathbf{c}_i f_i=\rho_0\mathbf{u}.
\]
The collision and source terms are then chosen so that the corresponding moment equations coincide with the incompressible system without requiring a low-Mach-number expansion.

This construction can improve upon entropic lattice Boltzmann methods in several respects. Entropic schemes impose a discrete entropy functional and determine the collision state through entropy minimization or an entropy-balance condition. Their principal benefit is nonlinear stabilization: they tend to preserve population positivity and suppress instabilities associated with under-resolved or low-viscosity flows. Nevertheless, standard entropic schemes generally retain the weakly compressible structure of conventional lattice Boltzmann models. Incompressibility is recovered only asymptotically as the lattice Mach number,
\[
\mathrm{Ma}=\frac{|\mathbf{u}|}{c_s},
\]
approaches zero. Consequently, pressure is linked to a small density variation through an equation of state, acoustic modes remain present, and the recovered momentum equation contains Mach-number and lattice-truncation corrections, commonly of order \(O(\mathrm{Ma}^2)\) under standard diffusive scaling.

By contrast, an inverse kinetic model may treat pressure as an independent kinetic moment and impose the divergence-free constraint through the exact moment hierarchy. It can therefore remove the conceptual need for artificial density fluctuations, a barotropic equation of state, and a Chapman–Enskog closure. It also permits forcing terms to be tailored to eliminate non-Galilean or lattice-isotropy defects at the macroscopic level. This greater freedom can provide exact kinetic consistency for finite values of the formal Mach parameter and can simplify the imposition of physical initial and boundary data. The improvement is primarily one of macroscopic fidelity, however, rather than automatic nonlinear stability. Unless an additional entropy or positivity structure is supplied, an inverse kinetic scheme need not inherit the robustness of entropic LB methods. Furthermore, exact recovery at the continuous kinetic level does not eliminate errors due to spatial discretization, time integration, velocity quadrature, interpolation, or boundary closure.

The comparison with Chorin’s artificial-compressibility method is particularly instructive. Chorin replaces the incompressibility constraint by an evolution equation such as
\[
\varepsilon\,\partial_t p+\nabla\!\cdot\mathbf{u}=0,
\]
where \(\varepsilon\) is the artificial-compressibility parameter. The incompressible equations are recovered only in the singular limit \(\varepsilon\to0\). For smooth, well-prepared solutions, the divergence defect and the associated macroscopic error are typically \(O(\varepsilon)\), although initial layers, boundaries, and the chosen temporal discretization can modify this estimate. Smaller \(\varepsilon\) also generates increasingly fast artificial pressure waves and may impose restrictive stability or conditioning requirements.

An exactly constructed inverse kinetic theory has a stronger consistency property: taking its prescribed moments yields
\[
\nabla\!\cdot\mathbf{u}=0
\]
and the Navier–Stokes momentum equation without an \(O(\varepsilon)\) artificial-compressibility remainder or an \(O(\mathrm{Ma}^2)\) weak-compressibility remainder. In that formal sense, it is not merely asymptotically accurate with respect to an incompressibility parameter; it is exact at the continuous kinetic-moment level. After numerical discretization, its observed accuracy is instead governed by the orders of the lattice, quadrature, time-stepping, and boundary algorithms:
\[
\|\mathbf{u}_h-\mathbf{u}\|
=O(\Delta x^{\,r}+\Delta t^{\,s})
\]
for an \(r\)-th-order spatial and \(s\)-th-order temporal implementation, subject to regularity and stability. Chorin’s method generally carries an additional modeling term,
\[
O(\varepsilon)+O(\Delta x^{\,r}+\Delta t^{\,s}),
\]
whereas a properly realized inverse kinetic method need not.

Thus, IKLBT can offer superior formal incompressible accuracy to both entropic LB and artificial-compressibility methods: it avoids the low-Mach asymptotics of the former and the \(\varepsilon\to0\) limit of the latter. Its practical superiority is not unconditional, however; it depends on whether the inverse forcing remains local and computationally tractable, whether stable and positive populations can be maintained, and whether the discrete implementation preserves the exact moment identities to the advertised order.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a physics journal abstract describing an exact LB inverse kinetic formulation, its freedom of realization, treatment of arbitrary smooth non-equilibrium states, boundary validity, and implications for conventional lattice Boltzmann accuracy estimates.
counterfactuals.output: We present an exact lattice-Boltzmann inverse kinetic formulation for prescribed smooth fluid evolution, in which a finite set of discrete kinetic populations is constructed so that selected velocity moments reproduce the target macroscopic fields and governing equations identically. The realization is non-unique: collision operators, source terms, kinetic equilibria, discrete velocities, and higher-order moments may be chosen within a broad equivalence class without altering the recovered hydrodynamics. Unlike asymptotic Chapman–Enskog-based schemes, the formulation does not require proximity to kinetic equilibrium, small Mach or Knudsen numbers, or weak departures from a reference state, and therefore applies to arbitrary smooth non-equilibrium distributions compatible with the assigned moments. Appropriate incoming-population rules provide an exact kinetic representation of initial and boundary data, including on the physical boundary, rather than only in the bulk or in an asymptotic boundary layer. This exact correspondence separates modeling error from discretization and implementation errors. Consequently, conventional lattice-Boltzmann accuracy estimates based on low-Mach expansions, hydrodynamic scaling, or finite-order equilibrium truncations are not intrinsic to the inverse kinetic description; they characterize only particular approximate realizations. The framework thus clarifies the freedom available in designing stable lattice-Boltzmann algorithms while providing a benchmark against which their consistency and accuracy can be assessed.
